entries.content:
### Convert lmms-eval JSON to MME-CoT Format

Source: https://github.com/evolvinglmms-lab/lmms-eval/blob/main/lmms_eval/tasks/mme_cot/README.md

Use the provided Python script to convert lmms-eval JSON outputs into the format required by the MME-CoT evaluation script. This script supports conversion for both CoT and direct prompts.

```python
# For CoT prompt
python tools/update_lmmseval_json.py \
--lmms_eval_json_path mmecot_reasoning_test_for_submission.json \
--save_path results/json/YOUR_MODEL_NAME_cot.json
# For direct prompt
python tools/update_lmmseval_json.py \
--lmms_eval_json_path mmecot_direct_test_for_submission.json \
--save_path results/json/YOUR_MODEL_NAME_dir.json
```

--------------------------------

### Resolved CLI Arguments in Results JSON

Source: https://github.com/evolvinglmms-lab/lmms-eval/blob/main/docs/releases/lmms-eval-0.7.md

Shows the structure of a results JSON file, including the 'resolved_cli_args' field which details the complete configuration after merging defaults, YAML, and CLI overrides.

```json
{
  "config": {
    "model": "qwen2_5_vl",
    "model_args": "pretrained=Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct,device_map=auto",
    "resolved_cli_args": {
      "model": "qwen2_5_vl",
      "model_args": "pretrained=Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct,device_map=auto",
      "tasks": "mme,mmmu_val",
      "batch_size": 1,
      "num_fewshot": 0,
      "seed": "42,42,42,42",
      "gen_kwargs": "temperature=0,max_new_tokens=1024",
      "output_path": "results/",
      "log_samples": true,
      "limit": null,
      "..."
    }
  }
}
```

--------------------------------

### Example JSONL Record for Logged Samples

Source: https://github.com/evolvinglmms-lab/lmms-eval/blob/main/docs/getting-started/commands.md

Illustrates the structure of a single JSON object within a JSONL file generated when the `--log_samples` flag is used. This record includes document ID, input prompt, target answer, raw and filtered model responses, document hash, and metric scores.

```json
{
  "doc_id": 0,
  "input": "What is shown in this image?\nAnswer with a single word.",
  "target": "cat",
  "resps": [["<think>\nThe image shows a small furry animal...\n</think>\ncat"]],
  "filtered_resps": ["cat"],
  "doc_hash": "a1b2c3d4e5...",
  "exact_match": 1.0
}
```

--------------------------------

### Example MEGA-Bench Evaluation Result

Source: https://github.com/evolvinglmms-lab/lmms-eval/blob/main/lmms_eval/tasks/megabench/README.md

This JSON structure represents the output of a MEGA-Bench evaluation, including model summary scores and keyword-based statistics for different skill categories.

```json
{
    "model_summary": {
        "core": {
            "num_eval_tasks": 440,
            "num_eval_samples": 6531,
            "macro_mean_score": 0.21890499112354772
        },
        "open": ...,
        "overall_score": 0.21890499112354772
    },
    "keyword_stats": {
        "skills": {
            "Object Recognition and Classification": {
                "count": 272,
                "num_samples": 4193,
                "tasks": [],
                "average_score": 0.237467941941504
            },
            "Domain-Specific Knowledge and Skills": {
                "count": 66,
                "num_samples": 1153,
                "tasks": [],
                "average_score": 0.2134904060117354
            },
            "Mathematical and Logical Reasoning": {

            },
```

### File Reference > eval > prompt_stability

Source: https://github.com/evolvinglmms-lab/lmms-eval/blob/main/test/README.md

Within the `eval` directory, the `prompt_stability` subdirectory contains tests for snapshot comparison and a collection of golden prompt files in JSON format.

entries.title: v0.34 Hashline Eval Drafts — 4 drafts created
entries.content:
## v0.34 Hashline Eval Drafts

Created 4 eval drafts under evals/drafts/ following docs/eval-writing-guide.md §0-2 and the Student-Agent Eval Draft Author prompt.

### Drafts

| ID | Category | Construct |
|---|---|---|
| hashline-recovery-001 | correctness | Consecutive file edit integrity via hash tag chaining — sequential edits on same file with correct tag propagation |
| hashline-signal-001 | integration | Rejection signal provenance integrity — stale-tag rejection produces signal with non-empty provenance and evidenceRef |
| hashline-snapshot-001 | correctness | Snapshot creation on file read — read_range creates SnapshotStore record with matching content tag |
| hashline-stale-reject-002 | safety | Batch stale edit rejection — 3 files externally modified, all stale-tag edits rejected independently |

### Each draft contains 8 files

spec.json, task/instruction.md, task/task.toml, task/environment/src/*.ts, task/tests/test.sh, task/solution/solve.sh, task/adversarial/README.md, review-notes.md

### Key risks identified in self-audit

1. All 4 drafts have grader-too-broad gap: structural tests verify final file content, not the Hashline mechanism (tag chaining, signal provenance, snapshot creation, stale rejection). Only Hashline integration tests can close this gap.
2. signal-001 and snapshot-001 require agent access to signal store / SnapshotStore API; harness must provide this.
3. stale-reject-002 requires harness to inject external file modifications after agent reads to trigger stale path.
4. signal-001 and snapshot-001 ask agent to write a report (signal-audit.md / snapshot-report.md); agent can fabricate reports. Only Hashline integration with write-protected stores resolves this.
5. All drafts are DRAFT status — NOT through ABA, verifier, trials, human review, or CommitGate.

### v0.34 case catalog coverage

12 cases in evals/hashline_cases.json. 5 now have drafts:
- hashline-stale-reject-001 → existing draft (hashline-stale-reject/)
- hashline-stale-reject-002 → new draft
- hashline-recovery-001 → new draft
- hashline-signal-001 → new draft
- hashline-snapshot-001 → new draft

7 cases without drafts: stale-reject-003 (partial tag match), recovery-002/003, signal-002, token-001, snapshot-002 (LRU eviction), coexist-001 (git SnapshotManager).

### Key project structure

- docs/eval-writing-guide.md: 5 gates, 8-file draft format, checklist
- evals/hashline_cases.json: 12 v0.34 scenario definitions
- evals/drafts/hashline-stale-reject/: pre-existing single-file stale reject draft
- evals/drafts/hashline-recovery-001/, signal-001/, snapshot-001/, stale-reject-002/: new drafts
